name: JSONSchemaBench: A Rigorous Benchmark of Structured Outputs for Language Models
problem: Constrained decoding has standardised on JSON Schema and grown in adoption, yet nobody has systematically evaluated whether the shipped frameworks actually WORK on real-world schemas, or what they cost.
mechanism: Not an inference method - an evaluation framework. Assesses constrained decoding along three dimensions: efficiency in generating constraint-compliant output, COVERAGE of constraint types (can the framework express them at all?), and QUALITY of what it emits. Ships JSONSchemaBench: 10K real-world JSON schemas spanning a wide range of constraints at varying complexity, paired with the official JSON Schema Test Suite for conformance checking. Evaluates six state-of-the-art frameworks: Guidance, Outlines, Llama.cpp, XGrammar, OpenAI, and Gemini - i.e. the actual production constrained-decoding stacks, not research prototypes.
speedup_reported: Not a speedup paper. Its finding is the one that matters for this repo: coverage of constraint types is INCOMPLETE across all six frameworks, so 'supports JSON Schema' is not a sufficient claim - a schema feature unsupported by the chosen engine fails silently or at request time. No single latency multiplier is claimed in the abstract and none is recorded here.
notes:
ADOPTION of the BENCHMARK: released publicly and usable against any constrained-decoding stack, which is why this record is the evaluation-infrastructure entry for the structured-output sub-area. THE KEY CROSS-RECORD FACT: this benchmark is the only place in the repo that evaluates Outlines, Guidance, XGrammar, and llama.cpp's grammar path SIDE BY SIDE on the same schemas - and Outlines and Guidance do NOT have arXiv preprints at all (both were searched for exhaustively via the arXiv API, by title, by author, and via the arXiv search UI; neither resolves), which is exactly why a benchmark paper matters more for them than a paper would. Every claim about structured-output engine coverage should be routed through this record rather than to a vendor page. VENUE NOTE: no venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar and no arXiv comment venue, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = ArXiv v1 (Jan 2025). hardware_relevance is empty because the benchmark measures framework overhead and correctness, not hardware-dependent speedup.

'unknown' is used here rather than leaving the field null or guessing 'main': the schema separates 'unknown' from 'main' precisely so that an unprereviewed preprint is not silently counted as main-track work. This annotation is what lets a downstream filter distinguish 'peer reviewed, main track' from 'not peer reviewed' without inferring it from the venue string.
